links.note: Was 31342 'Splitting into tens and units', which is the (20+3)^2 expansion trick for computing a square in full. This item wants only the unit place of 5278 squared, decided by 8 squared ending in 4 - the ending-digit property, 31338.

Was 31348 'Counting the subtractions', which is finding a square ROOT by subtracting successive odd numbers - the opposite direction from this item. Asking how many zeros 400 squared ends with is a question about how a square terminates, so 31338.

Was 31347 'Every square is a sum of odd numbers', a statement about decomposing a square, not about parity. Whether a square comes out odd is settled by the base's last digit, which is 31338 - the same concept as the matching 'would be even' item qid 113582.

Was 31334 'A number multiplied by itself', which is only the definition of a square number. The item needs 90 = 2 x 3^2 x 5 factorised and its unpaired 2 and 5 supplied, i.e. the prime-factor pairing of 31349 - where the matching 'divide 48' item qid 113593 sits.

Was 31351 'How many digits the root will have'. The item asks for the one's DIGIT of the root of 625, not how many digits it has; 625 ending in 5 forces a root ending in 5, which is the ending-digit property 31338.

Was 31333 'Where the name comes from', i.e. that squaring is named after the square's area. The item actually asks for the SIDE of a square of area 441, and the set has a concept for exactly that: 31346, whose own example is a square of area 144 having side 12.

Was 31347 'Every square is a sum of odd numbers'. With the key False, the truncated statement is that the sum of two perfect squares is itself a perfect square - a different claim entirely from a square being a run of consecutive odd numbers. Nothing in the set is about sums of two squares.

Was 31347 'Every square is a sum of odd numbers'. The item is the True/False claim that n squared always exceeds n, which is false at n = 1. No concept in the set compares a square with the number itself, so there is nothing to move it to.
